currentContext.strengths: Strong brand equity led by the Fortune brand, one of India's most recognised food brands, generating ` 30,000+ crore in revenues|Nationwide distribution network ensuring deep market penetration (2.6 million total retail reach, 9,65,000+ direct outlets, 60,000+ rural towns)|Large-scale refining infrastructure with ~25% share of India's refining capacity|Integrated sourcing capabilities supported by Wilmar Group's global procurement network|Operational scale enabling logistics efficiency and high-frequency replenishment across markets|Presence across all key consumption oils enabling broad market participation|Multi-tier brand architecture spanning super premium (Fortune Xpert, Fortune Premio), premium/flagship (Fortune) and mass (Kings, Aadhar, Raag) segments
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen edible oil leadership while accelerating growth in Food & FMCG and moving up the value curve in Industry Essentials|Leverage the integrated business model — global sourcing, extensive manufacturing infrastructure, pan-India distribution reach, deep rural penetration, strong retailer relationships and risk management — to efficiently introduce new products and scale emerging businesses|'Scaling India's Food Essentials' — extend the trust, distribution and infrastructure built in edible oils to a broader portfolio of packaged staples (wheat flour, rice, pulses, besan, sugar)|Continue to invest in talent, technology and governance that sustain long-term performance|Evaluate selective acquisitions in regional staple brands that complement the portfolio and can benefit from national distribution reach|Enhance the portfolio through value-added offerings centred on health, nutrition and convenience|Strengthen position across staples while expanding presence in higher-growth and higher-value Food & FMCG segments to improve quality of earnings|AWL follows a disciplined, balanced capital allocation approach: the Board remains focused on investing for future growth (funding capex such as the Gohana food complex substantially from IPO proceeds) while being mindful of delivering returns to shareholders responsibly. FY25-26 saw the Board recommend the Company's first dividend since listing, reflecting confidence in long-term prospects, balance sheet strength and cash flow generation; a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A) is in place and published on the Company's website.
currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 marked a defining phase in AWL's capital programme, led by the Gohana integrated food complex in Haryana — AWL's largest-ever greenfield project, spanning approximately 80 acres, funded largely through IPO proceeds. Commissioned in FY25, rice and mustard oil operations are running, with wheat flour and milling capacity being brought online progressively; the site is designed to process a diverse range of food products (rice, mustard oil, wheat flour, suji, rawa, maida) under one roof. AWL also commenced castor derivatives capacity at its existing castor facility in Mundra, expanding its presence in value-added castor-based products within Industry Essentials. Across the wider manufacturing network, targeted capacity additions in wheat flour, pulses, besan and castor derivatives have strengthened AWL's presence in high-growth, higher-margin sub-categories. At Vidisha, deeper integration across the soya value chain — from crushing to nuggets, flakes and textured vegetable protein — has improved value capture and expanded the protein/nutrition portfolio. Separately, the Company completed the first tranche of the acquisition of GD Foods Manufacturing (India) Private Limited (an 80% equity stake, owner of the 'Tops' brand), strengthening its presence in higher-margin, value-added food categories, and continues to scale Omkar Chemicals (acquired 2024, oleochemicals) with volumes doubling and revenues crossing ` 300 crore during the year.
currentContext.mdna: Structural rise in India's packaged-food consumption: per capita GDP and packaged-food spending are rising (per capita packaged food spend grew from ~`4,800 in 2020 to ~`7,600 in 2025), driving a shift from loose to branded/packaged staples|Structural trends supporting long-term growth: premiumisation across food categories, increasing preference for trusted brands, growing penetration of packaged staples, rising focus on food safety and quality, continued growth in rural consumption, expansion of modern trade/e-commerce/quick commerce, and rising demand for health and convenience offerings|Alternate channels — quick commerce, HoReCa and branded exports — are emerging as major growth engines, complementing traditional trade|Edible oil prices firmed in the second half of FY26 due to West Asia geopolitical developments, rising freight costs and vessel tightness, creating near-term sourcing and consumption challenges that the Company's integrated, diversified model helped absorb|Company's long-term strategy is centred on leveraging edible oil leadership to build a broader, trusted food essentials platform, with the Fortune brand's household trust as the core lever

risks.note: As a large importer and processor of edible oils, prices are influenced by weather patterns, geopolitical developments, supply-demand imbalances and regulatory changes, which can impact procurement costs, margins and overall profitability.
Significant exposure to imports of crude edible oils and other overseas transactions creates currency exposure that must be managed from the point of purchase/shipment onward.

Arises from sourcing, inventory management, project execution and process efficiency across a large-scale, integrated value chain; can impact continuity, cost structures and execution timelines if not managed effectively.
Inherent in an increasingly digital operating environment, with potential implications for data security, system integrity and business continuity.
Risk of control override and loss of financial integrity across operations; managed through a control environment with structured systems, defined authority levels and independent oversight.

one-line thesis: AWL delivered record Q4 revenue and profitability driven by 17% edible oil volume growth and 40% EBITDA expansion, with strong brand performance and channel diversification offsetting macro headwinds; the company is prioritizing volume-led food segment growth over margins in FY27, targeting mid-teens growth and structural margin expansion post-FY28.
financial scorecard: revenue: +18% YoY (INR21,000cr); EBITDA/margin: +40% YoY (INR628cr, 30% EBITDA margin); PAT (rptd): +54% YoY (INR293cr); PAT (normalized): +50% YoY (ex-G2G); order book: Not disclosed; net debt: Inventory down, trade credit up — net debt position stable, current assets/liabilities balanced
guidance: revenue growth: 15-17% FY27; margin: Food EBITDA neutral till FY27, target INR1,500-2,000/ton EBITDA from FY28; order inflow: Double-digit food volume growth expected; capex/commissioning: Krishnapatnam oleochemical plant commissioning in Q4FY27
segment / subsidiary detail: Edible Oil: 17% volume growth, INR17,520cr revenue, 60bps market share gain; Food & FMCG: 6% volume growth (3% normalized ex-G2G), 5.4% wheat flour MS, 9% basmati rice MS; Industry Essentials: 13% volume growth, oleochemicals 30% of segment, specialty chemicals 7-8%; GD Foods: 24% Q4 volume growth, 55% margin
growth verticals / optionality: Alternate channels (15% of edible oil volume, growing at 43% YoY); premiumization (Fortune Premio, cold press oils); HoReCa (64% YoY growth); branded exports (48% YoY growth); rural distribution (55K new outlets every 3 months); rice/wheat/besan/sugar/pulses as key volume drivers
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin per ton: INR12,000 (Q4), INR11,500 (FY26); EBITDA per ton: INR3,400 (Q4), INR3,500 (FY26); cost pressures: March crude oil +10%, packing material +10-15% (impact delayed to Q1FY27); rupee depreciation added import cost pressure
capex / expansion: Krishnapatnam oleochemical plant (Q4FY27 commissioning); no new plantation capex planned; capex focused on distribution, logistics, and specialty chemical capacity
capital allocation: Prioritizing volume growth in food segment; reinvesting EBITDA into distribution expansion, premium product launches, and alternate channel logistics; no dividend or buyback guidance; debt used for working capital flexibility
risks & watch-items: Edible oil price volatility; rupee depreciation; LPG supply disruptions impacting HoReCa; food segment margin compression from aggressive volume growth; competitive pressure from private labels in wheat/rice; geopolitical supply chain risks
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined — management emphasizes structural growth over short-term margin gains, acknowledges macro headwinds but highlights brand strength and distribution scale as moats; tone is optimistic on FY27 volume-led growth and post-FY28 margin expansion
non-obvious takeaways: Despite 18% revenue growth, EBITDA margin expansion was driven by volume leverage, not pricing power; 43% alternate channel growth is from a low base (15% of edible oil volume), but profitability is 50-60bps higher than general trade; food segment’s 3% normalized growth masks a 6% underlying growth excluding one-off G2G business; 9% basmati rice market share is a key hidden win in a fragmented market

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

one_liner.body: India's largest branded edible oil company, anchored by the Fortune brand, evolving into a diversified Food & FMCG and Industry Essentials platform.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: AWL Agri Business Limited (formerly Adani Wilmar Limited) operates an integrated agri-based ecosystem spanning Edible Oils (branded cooking oils across soyabean, mustard, sunflower, rice bran, palm and specialty oils), Food & FMCG (packaged staples such as rice, wheat flour, pulses, sugar, besan, soya nuggets, poha and sauces/condiments), and Industry Essentials (value-added oleochemicals and industrial/export-oriented products). It serves millions of Indian households and food manufacturers, backed by shared sourcing, refining and distribution infrastructure and Wilmar Group's global procurement network.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Edible Oil: 17% volume growth, INR17,520cr revenue, 60bps market share gain; Food & FMCG: 6% volume growth (3% normalized ex-G2G), 5.4% wheat flour MS, 9% basmati rice MS; Industry Essentials: 13% volume growth, oleochemicals 30% of segment, specialty chemicals 7-8%; GD Foods: 24% Q4 volume growth, 55% margin

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: 15-17% FY27; margin: Food EBITDA neutral till FY27, target INR1,500-2,000/ton EBITDA from FY28; order inflow: Double-digit food volume growth expected; capex/commissioning: Krishnapatnam oleochemical plant commissioning in Q4FY27

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Alternate channels (15% of edible oil volume, growing at 43% YoY); premiumization (Fortune Premio, cold press oils); HoReCa (64% YoY growth); branded exports (48% YoY growth); rural distribution (55K new outlets every 3 months); rice/wheat/besan/sugar/pulses as key volume drivers

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural rise in India's packaged-food consumption: per capita GDP and packaged-food spending are rising (per capita packaged food spend grew from ~`4,800 in 2020 to ~`7,600 in 2025), driving a shift from loose to branded/packaged staples
- Structural trends supporting long-term growth: premiumisation across food categories, increasing preference for trusted brands, growing penetration of packaged staples, rising focus on food safety and quality, continued growth in rural consumption, expansion of modern trade/e-commerce/quick commerce, and rising demand for health and convenience offerings
- Alternate channels — quick commerce, HoReCa and branded exports — are emerging as major growth engines, complementing traditional trade
- Edible oil prices firmed in the second half of FY26 due to West Asia geopolitical developments, rising freight costs and vessel tightness, creating near-term sourcing and consumption challenges that the Company's integrated, diversified model helped absorb
- Company's long-term strategy is centred on leveraging edible oil leadership to build a broader, trusted food essentials platform, with the Fortune brand's household trust as the core lever

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin per ton: INR12,000 (Q4), INR11,500 (FY26); EBITDA per ton: INR3,400 (Q4), INR3,500 (FY26); cost pressures: March crude oil +10%, packing material +10-15% (impact delayed to Q1FY27); rupee depreciation added import cost pressure

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing volume growth in food segment; reinvesting EBITDA into distribution expansion, premium product launches, and alternate channel logistics; no dividend or buyback guidance; debt used for working capital flexibility

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 marked a defining phase in AWL's capital programme, led by the Gohana integrated food complex in Haryana — AWL's largest-ever greenfield project, spanning approximately 80 acres, funded largely through IPO proceeds. Commissioned in FY25, rice and mustard oil operations are running, with wheat flour and milling capacity being brought online progressively; the site is designed to process a diverse range of food products (rice, mustard oil, wheat flour, suji, rawa, maida) under one roof. AWL also commenced castor derivatives capacity at its existing castor facility in Mundra, expanding its presence in value-added castor-based products within Industry Essentials. Across the wider manufacturing network, targeted capacity additions in wheat flour, pulses, besan and castor derivatives have strengthened AWL's presence in high-growth, higher-margin sub-categories. At Vidisha, deeper integration across the soya value chain — from crushing to nuggets, flakes and textured vegetable protein — has improved value capture and expanded the protein/nutrition portfolio. Separately, the Company completed the first tranche of the acquisition of GD Foods Manufacturing (India) Private Limited (an 80% equity stake, owner of the 'Tops' brand), strengthening its presence in higher-margin, value-added food categories, and continues to scale Omkar Chemicals (acquired 2024, oleochemicals) with volumes doubling and revenues crossing ` 300 crore during the year.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined — management emphasizes structural growth over short-term margin gains, acknowledges macro headwinds but highlights brand strength and distribution scale as moats; tone is optimistic on FY27 volume-led growth and post-FY28 margin expansion

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong brand equity led by the Fortune brand, one of India's most recognised food brands, generating ` 30,000+ crore in revenues
- Nationwide distribution network ensuring deep market penetration (2.6 million total retail reach, 9,65,000+ direct outlets, 60,000+ rural towns)
- Large-scale refining infrastructure with ~25% share of India's refining capacity
- Integrated sourcing capabilities supported by Wilmar Group's global procurement network
- Operational scale enabling logistics efficiency and high-frequency replenishment across markets
- Presence across all key consumption oils enabling broad market participation
- Multi-tier brand architecture spanning super premium (Fortune Xpert, Fortune Premio), premium/flagship (Fortune) and mass (Kings, Aadhar, Raag) segments

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Edible oil price volatility; rupee depreciation; LPG supply disruptions impacting HoReCa; food segment margin compression from aggressive volume growth; competitive pressure from private labels in wheat/rice; geopolitical supply chain risks

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite 18% revenue growth, EBITDA margin expansion was driven by volume leverage, not pricing power; 43% alternate channel growth is from a low base (15% of edible oil volume), but profitability is 50-60bps higher than general trade; food segment’s 3% normalized growth masks a 6% underlying growth excluding one-off G2G business; 9% basmati rice market share is a key hidden win in a fragmented market

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen edible oil leadership while accelerating growth in Food & FMCG and moving up the value curve in Industry Essentials
- Leverage the integrated business model — global sourcing, extensive manufacturing infrastructure, pan-India distribution reach, deep rural penetration, strong retailer relationships and risk management — to efficiently introduce new products and scale emerging businesses
- 'Scaling India's Food Essentials' — extend the trust, distribution and infrastructure built in edible oils to a broader portfolio of packaged staples (wheat flour, rice, pulses, besan, sugar)
- Continue …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Rebranding] The company is AWL Agri Business Limited, formerly known as Adani Wilmar Limited.
- [Disclosure change] Effective Q1FY27, Food & FMCG performance is presented on a margin basis (revenue, EBITDA, EBITDA%), while Edible Oils & Industry Essentials continue on a per-ton basis; company-level disclosure adds normalised gross profit & EBITDA, segment-wise EBITDA and segment-wise ROCE.
- [Accounting] Since Q4FY24 results, derivative gain/loss has been reclassified from 'Cost of Material Consumed' to 'Other Income / Other Expenses'; normalised EBITDA regroups this commodity derivative impact.
- [Regulation] Edible oil pack sizes will be standardized as per the latest notification of Government of India, and duty-free imports from Nepal continue.
- [Macro] Sea freight costs doubled at the peak of geopolitical disruptions and remain ~50% above pre-war levels; Indonesia's B50 is expected to divert volumes out of annual palm oil demand from July; rainfall was 32% below normal as of 15 June, raising supply and rural-demand risk.
